title: 09. Evaluation: Evaluation & Metrics
summary: RAGAS (Retrieval-Augmented Generation Assessment) is the industry-standard framework for evaluating RAG systems. It provides reference-free metrics (no human labels required) by using an LLM as a judge.

sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body: RAGAS (Retrieval-Augmented Generation Assessment) is the industry-standard framework for evaluating RAG systems. It provides reference-free metrics (no human labels required) by using an LLM as a judge. The four core RAGAS metrics form a 2×2 matrix: retrieval quality (context precision, context recall) and generation quality (faithfulness, answer relevancy). Each metric targets a specific failure mode: poor context precision means retrieved chunks are irrelevant noise; poor context recall means relevant chunks were missed; poor faithfulness means the LLM hallucinated beyond the context; poor answer relevancy means the answer doesn't address the question.

sections.title: ④ Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
RAGAS METRICS — 2×2 QUALITY MATRIX
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

                    RETRIEVAL QUALITY
                Low Precision    High Precision
               ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  High    │ Low Precision,   │  High Precision,        │
  Recall  │ High Recall      │  High Recall            │
          │ (Over-retrieval) │  (Optimal)              │
          │ Too many chunks, │  Right chunks,          │
 R        │ many irrelevant  │  nothing missing        │
 E        ├──────────────────┼──────────────────────────┤
 C  Low   │ Low Precision,   │  High Precision,        │
 A  Recall│ Low Recall       │  Low Recall             │
 L        │ (Both bad)       │  (Under-retrieval)      │
 L        │ Wrong chunks AND │  Relevant chunks only,  │
          │ missing answers  │  but missing some      │
          └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

METRIC DEFINITIONS WITH EXAMPLES:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FAITHFULNESS: "Is the answer grounded in retrieved context?"

Context: "Warranty period is 2 years"
Answer (faithful):   "The warranty is 2 years [Doc 1]" → score: 1.0
Answer (unfaithful): "The warranty is 2 years, and extended to 3 years for Pro users"
                     → "extended to 3 years for Pro users" NOT in context → score: 0.5

ANSWER RELEVANCY: "Does the answer address the question?"

Question: "What is the warranty period?"
Answer (relevant):   "The warranty period is 2 years" → score: 1.0
Answer (irrelevant): "Our warranty covers manufacturing defects and includes 
                      free shipping for replacements" → addresses warranty TYPE 
                      not warranty PERIOD → score: 0.6

CONTEXT PRECISION: "Are retrieved chunks relevant?"

Retrieved: [warranty chunk ✓, contact info chunk ✗, pricing chunk ✗]
Precision = 1/3 = 0.33 (bad! too many irrelevant chunks)

Retrieved: [warranty chunk ✓, warranty FAQ chunk ✓]
Precision = 2/2 = 1.00 (good!)

CONTEXT RECALL: "Were the necessary chunks retrieved?"

Reference answer needs: warranty period + exclusions + claim process
Retrieved covers: warranty period ✓, exclusions ✓ (missed claim process ✗)
Recall = 2/3 = 0.67 (needs improvement)

EVALUATION WORKFLOW:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Test Set (100 Q&A pairs)
    │
    ▼ Run RAG Pipeline
(100 answers + contexts generated)
    │
    ▼ RAGAS Evaluation (LLM Judge)
┌────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Faithfulness:      0.91 ✅         │
│ Answer Relevancy:  0.88 ✅         │
│ Context Precision: 0.72 ❌ < 0.75 │  ← Over-retrieval problem!
│ Context Recall:    0.83 ✅         │
└────────────────────────────────────┘
    │
    ▼ Regression Check vs Baseline
Context Precision: 0.72 < baseline 0.82 (regression: -0.10)
    │
    ▼ CI/CD Gate: FAIL
Deploy blocked → engineer investigates chunking or K value
```

quiz.question: Explain each of the four core RAGAS metrics and what failure mode each detects.
options: Retrieval-only metrics: (1) Self-retrieval — embed a chunk, retrieve it, check if it's in top-1 (should always be 1.0); (2) Manual spot-check — human reviewer rates…
LLM-as-Judge uses a powerful LLM (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5) to score RAG answers on custom criteria: accuracy, completeness, tone, citation quality.
Offline: batch evaluation on a static test set before deployment.
Faithfulness: #supported_claims / #total_claims. Detects LLM hallucination — claims in the answer not supported by retrieved context.
quiz.explanation: Faithfulness: #supported_claims / #total_claims. Detects LLM hallucination — claims in the answer not supported by retrieved context. Answer Relevancy: Cosine similarity between the question and AI-generated questions about the answer.

quiz.question: How do you create a RAG evaluation test set without human annotation?
options: MTEB (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark) evaluates embedding models across 56 tasks: retrieval, classification, clustering, etc.
LLM-as-Judge uses a powerful LLM (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5) to score RAG answers on custom criteria: accuracy, completeness, tone, citation quality.
BEIR (Benchmarking Information Retrieval) is a collection of 18 heterogeneous datasets (scientific papers, financial news, biomedical text, etc.) for evaluating…
Use synthetic data generation: (1) LLM-generated Q&A from corpus — for each chunk, ask an LLM to generate a relevant question and answer; (2) Question diversity:…
quiz.explanation: Use synthetic data generation: (1) LLM-generated Q&A from corpus — for each chunk, ask an LLM to generate a relevant question and answer; (2) Question diversity: generate factual, comparative, and procedural questions; (3) Negative examples: generate questions your system should NOT answer (outside scope). This creates an automated test harness. --- Q4–Q10 Summary:

quiz.question: What is LLM-as-Judge and how does it differ from RAGAS?
options: Offline: batch evaluation on a static test set before deployment.
Retrieval-only metrics: (1) Self-retrieval — embed a chunk, retrieve it, check if it's in top-1 (should always be 1.0); (2) Manual spot-check — human reviewer rates…
BEIR (Benchmarking Information Retrieval) is a collection of 18 heterogeneous datasets (scientific papers, financial news, biomedical text, etc.) for evaluating…
LLM-as-Judge uses a powerful LLM (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5) to score RAG answers on custom criteria: accuracy, completeness, tone, citation quality.
quiz.explanation: LLM-as-Judge uses a powerful LLM (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5) to score RAG answers on custom criteria: accuracy, completeness, tone, citation quality. RAGAS is a specific framework with standardized metrics. LLM-as-Judge is more flexible (custom rubrics) but less reproducible.

quiz.question: What is MTEB and why is it relevant to RAG?
options: LLM-as-Judge uses a powerful LLM (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5) to score RAG answers on custom criteria: accuracy, completeness, tone, citation quality.
Retrieval-only metrics: (1) Self-retrieval — embed a chunk, retrieve it, check if it's in top-1 (should always be 1.0); (2) Manual spot-check — human reviewer rates…
Use synthetic data generation: (1) LLM-generated Q&A from corpus — for each chunk, ask an LLM to generate a relevant question and answer; (2) Question diversity:…
MTEB (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark) evaluates embedding models across 56 tasks: retrieval, classification, clustering, etc.
quiz.explanation: MTEB (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark) evaluates embedding models across 56 tasks: retrieval, classification, clustering, etc. The retrieval tasks (BEIR, NFCorpus, HotpotQA) are directly relevant to RAG — they measure how well an embedding model retrieves the correct documents for a query. Use MTEB scores to select embedding models before deployment.

quiz.question: What is BEIR and how do you use it for RAG benchmarking?
options: Three-layer monitoring: (1) Infrastructure metrics — latency P50/P95/P99, throughput, error rate, vector DB query time; (2) Retrieval metrics — average retrieved docs,…
Retrieval-only metrics: (1) Self-retrieval — embed a chunk, retrieve it, check if it's in top-1 (should always be 1.0); (2) Manual spot-check — human reviewer rates…
LLM-as-Judge uses a powerful LLM (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5) to score RAG answers on custom criteria: accuracy, completeness, tone, citation quality.
BEIR (Benchmarking Information Retrieval) is a collection of 18 heterogeneous datasets (scientific papers, financial news, biomedical text, etc.) for evaluating…
quiz.explanation: BEIR (Benchmarking Information Retrieval) is a collection of 18 heterogeneous datasets (scientific papers, financial news, biomedical text, etc.) for evaluating retrieval systems. Test your retrieval pipeline against BEIR datasets that match your domain. If your BEIR score is low on the target domain dataset, your embedding model or chunking strategy needs improvement.
